theorems.name: NobleFoundation.FirstProjection.interpreterGraph_wellFormed

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.FirstProjection.interpreterGraph_noEq
theorems.claim: the interpreter graph has no equality node

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.FirstProjection.interpreter_value

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.FirstProjection.specialize_noEq

theorems.claim: the specialized and annihilated residual still computes the program for every dynamic input

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.FirstProjection.unselected_branches_are_dead
theorems.claim: for every program exactly the selected operation node of each instruction is live in the residual

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.log2_go_eq
theorems.claim: the fuel-bounded logarithm equals the core floor logarithm whenever the fuel covers the input

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.log2_eq
theorems.claim: the model log2 is the core floor logarithm

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.log2_bracket
theorems.claim: the model log2 of a positive input brackets it between consecutive powers of two

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.floorLog2Ratio_lower
theorems.claim: for every positive input 2^floorLog2Ratio times the denominator is at most the numerator

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.floorLog2Ratio_upper
theorems.claim: off the power boundary the numerator is strictly below 2^(floorLog2Ratio+1) times the denominator

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.floorLog2Ratio_boundary
theorems.claim: on the power boundary the ratio is exactly 2^(floorLog2Ratio+1)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scaled_ratio
theorems.claim: the scaled quotient is the exact ratio times 2^(23 - floorLog2Ratio)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_powers
theorems.claim: the scale exponents combine to 2^23 at the lower and 2^24 at the upper bin edge

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_lower
theorems.claim: the lower normal-bin scale premise holds for every positive input

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_upper
theorems.claim: the upper normal-bin scale premise holds for every positive input off the power boundary

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_at_boundary
theorems.claim: on the power boundary the scaled quotient is exactly 2^24 times its denominator

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.upper_premise_fails_for_one_half
theorems.claim: the upper scale premise is not universal: 1/2 is on the power boundary and fails it

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.boundary_rounded
theorems.claim: on the power boundary the rounded significand is exactly 2^24

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.boundary_rounds_exactly
theorems.claim: on the power boundary the carried normal result is the exact ratio

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.roundPositive_absolute_error
theorems.claim: every positive input with a normal-range carried exponent has the half-ulp absolute bound, with no scale premise

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.roundPositive_relative_error
theorems.claim: every positive input with a normal-range carried exponent has the 2^-24 relative bound, with no scale or bin premise

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.absolute_error_covers_one_half
theorems.claim: at 1/2, where the upper premise fails, the result is exact and the absolute bound holds

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.adjointAfterWith_stepCoefficient

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGradientWith_stepCoefficient

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGraph_mulOwnValue_caught
theorems.claim: a multiplication rule that pairs each operand with its own value moves both slot gradients off the tangents

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGraph_addDropsSecond_caught
theorems.claim: an addition rule that drops its second operand moves both slot gradients off the tangents

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGraph_repeatedCountedOnce_caught
theorems.claim: counting a repeated multiplication operand once moves the slot behind it off its tangent while the other slot stays correct

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGraph_overwrite_caught
theorems.claim: overwriting adjoints instead of accumulating moves both slot gradients off the tangents

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.subGraph_wellFormed
theorems.claim: the non-index-aligned subtraction fixture is well formed

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.subGraph_value
theorems.claim: the subtraction fixture computes (x - y)^2 = 1 at x = 3, y = 2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.subGraph_tangents
theorems.claim: the subtraction fixture tangents are 2 along x and -2 along y

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.subGraph_derivative_slot_one
theorems.claim: the y tangent of the subtraction fixture is the Mathlib derivative

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.subGraph_slotGradients_match_tangents
theorems.claim: the model sweep gives the subtraction fixture slot gradients 2 and -2, its tangents

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.subGraph_subSignFlipped_caught
theorems.claim: a subtraction rule with the wrong second-operand sign moves the y gradient to 2 where the derivative is -2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.step_iff_wordRule

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.run_complete
theorems.claim: every Accounts derivation is a checker acceptance

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.run_iff_judged
theorems.claim: the checker decides the independent judgment exactly

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.step_preserves_agreement
theorems.claim: one step preserves eligibility agreement on the stacks it admits in both arms

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.joined_sequence_admission_agrees
theorems.claim: on a straight-line program two eligibility-agreeing stacks are admitted in both arms or neither and leave agreeing stacks

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.joined_judgment_transfers
theorems.claim: a straight-line judgment carries over to any eligibility-agreeing start with agreeing results

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.equal_length_does_not_lift
theorems.claim: equal-length stacks that disagree on eligibility separate a straight-line dup

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.lift_fixture
theorems.claim: stacks with different owners but agreeing eligibility run a three-word sequence alike and agree again

theorems.claim: for every positive input the numerator is at most 2^(floorLog2Ratio+1) times the denominator

theorems.claim: below the normal range the subnormal numerator a * 2^149 is at most 2^23 denominators

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_significand_bound
theorems.claim: below the normal range the rounded subnormal significand is at most 2^23

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_subnormal
theorems.claim: below the normal range roundPositive is the rounded significand capped at the smallest normal

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_eq_significand
theorems.claim: below the normal range the cap never changes the rounded significand

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_scaledMagnitude
theorems.claim: a significand below 2^23 encodes the subnormal n * 2^-149

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.smallest_normal_scaledMagnitude
theorems.claim: the significand 2^23 encodes the smallest normal with value 2^23 * 2^-149

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.small_encoding_not_negative
theorems.claim: a significand of at most 2^23 encodes a positive sign

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.exactValue_small
theorems.claim: every significand of at most 2^23 encodes exactly n * 2^-149

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_subnormal_absolute_error
